objective: Train a storm-focused probabilistic model from five-minute L1 solar-wind observations, prioritize G3+ detection, and evaluate every claim on a never-seen 2024–2026 interval.

resolution.input: Every valid five-minute OMNI solar-wind record is used to construct the predictors.
resolution.target: Definitive planetary Kp has one official value per fixed three-hour interval; a minute-by-minute Kp label does not exist.
resolution.independence: Counts and confidence intervals use three-hour bins or contiguous storm episodes, never millions of repeated five-minute pseudo-labels.
resolution.higherCadenceOption: GFZ Hp30 can support a separate 30-minute response-timing study, but it is not the official NOAA G scale target.
resolution.incumbentLimitation: Kp is the internationally recognised incumbent, but its three-hour aggregation blurs onset time and sub-bin peaks; it limits how precisely any Kp model can be trained and scored in time.

upstream.role: Five-minute L1 IMF and plasma values; OMNI Timeshift is used only to reconstruct issue time.
upstream.caveat: OMNI phase-front shifting is a retrospective propagation reference; it is not an independent bow-shock detector.

noaaForecast.selection: 0030 UTC issue only; next-day and two-day target columns

method.issueTime: OMNI target timestamp minus OMNI Timeshift; Timeshift is excluded from model features.
method.arrival: Issue time plus MRU travel from measured spacecraft X to a 13.5 Re bow-shock nose.
method.features: Five-minute speed, IMF, density and pressure summarized with southward-field, Newell, epsilon and viscous coupling features plus causal 3–9 h memory.
method.model: Separate gradient-boosted probability models for G1+ and G3+, plus a storm-weighted Kp regressor.
method.selection: Four expanding chronological validation folds from 2001–2023 select tree complexity and alert thresholds; 2024+ remains untouched.
method.eventDefinition: One or more contiguous official Kp bins at or above 5 (G1+) or 7 (G3+).
method.eventMatching: One-to-one chronological overlap matching with a predeclared ±3 h tolerance.

historicalKp.overviewAggregation: Maximum Kp in each UTC calendar month.
historicalKp.yearAggregation: Maximum Kp across the eight official three-hour bins in each UTC day.

coverage.caveat: Complete definitive record used as the reference series.
The local archived nowcast starts in 2025; blank earlier years mean unavailable, not quiet.
1995-2023 is an in-development hindcast; only 2024 onward is independent held-out evaluation.

kpSources.name: NOAA 3-day Kp forecast
kpSources.timing: Issued ahead of the target day (roughly 0–72 h)
kpSources.reason: Separately scored from immutable 0030 UTC archive issues on common 2025–2026 bins; not mixed into the 2024+ headline score.

kpSources.name: HelioSat GBDT candidate
kpSources.reason: Scored on every eligible held-out bin against GFZ definitive Kp.

kpSources.name: NOAA estimated planetary Kp
kpSources.timing: During or after the target interval; no positive forecast lead
kpSources.reason: It is an estimate of the response already occurring, not a like-for-like forecast.

kpSources.name: GFZ Kp nowcast
kpSources.timing: Available around/after interval completion; no L1 warning time
kpSources.reason: Separately scored as a no-lead reference ceiling on the same common bins; not presented as a forecast.

kpSources.name: GFZ definitive Kp
kpSources.reason: Independent ground-response target used for all headline scores.

scope.fairness: All four products are scored on the exact same bins against GFZ definitive Kp.

products.name: NOAA next-day forecast
products.timing: 23.5-44.5 h lead from the fixed 0030 UTC issue

products.name: NOAA two-day forecast
products.timing: 47.5-68.5 h lead from the fixed 0030 UTC issue

products.name: GFZ archived nowcast
products.timing: no positive forecast lead; archived provisional value

strongestWindow.title: Strongest definitive-Kp interval in held-out evaluation · 2024-05-11

limitations: The official Kp target is three-hourly; five-minute inputs improve feature fidelity but do not create additional independent storm labels.
Only 2024 onward is used for the final score, and no parameter or alert threshold is changed after viewing it.
The candidate is retrospective and must accumulate immutable live issue-time forecasts before operational performance can be claimed.
G3+ remains rare, so its event confidence intervals are materially wider than G1+ intervals even after extending to 1995.
OMNI uses retrospective phase-front processing; forward validation with the actual live L1 feed remains essential.
